info.title: Skill Registry API
info.description:
A self-hosted Registry for Agent Skills. This is the contract the CLI depends on; the web interface uses the same routes and has no private data path of its own.

**Conventions.** Every JSON key on the wire is snake_case, which means wire keys line up with Postgres column names. TypeScript types, interfaces, and classes are camelCase, so conversion happens once at the boundary in the shared module rather than ad hoc per call site.

**Artifact bytes never pass through this API.** Publishing returns a presigned upload target that the caller writes to directly, and reading an Artifact redirects to a short-lived presigned location. The API therefore validates the metadata a caller claims about a Skill, never the Artifact itself (ADR-0001).

get.description: Tells the web interface whether to show the bootstrap screen or the login screen. Unauthenticated, as the Skill reads are (ADR-0013).

initialized.description: False only while no User exists at all.

post.description:
Creates the first User, who is a Superadmin and chooses their own password. Available only while no User exists; afterwards this returns 409 forever and new Users come from `POST /users` instead.

Modelled as its own resource rather than as an unauthenticated `POST /users`, because the two differ in authentication, in who picks the password, and in whether a role may be supplied — one endpoint with two request shapes would be a trap for both callers. This is deliberately not a `Registry` resource: the Registry is the deployment itself, not something with a create-or-initialise lifecycle — this route is about the first User existing, nothing else.

201.description: The first User was created as a Superadmin and is logged in

409.description: A User already exists, so setup is closed

post.summary: Sign in with an email address and password
post.description:
Served by Better Auth (ADR-0016) rather than by a route in this codebase, and documented here because it is how the interface logs in. Issues a session and sets its cookie; the session is a row, so it can be revoked (ADR-0005's trade-off no longer applies).

An unknown email and a wrong password are refused identically, and both run an argon2id hash — the decoy for an unknown email costs what a real verify costs — so the two cannot be told apart by timing either.

If the User has `must_change_password` set, every route except reading and replacing their own password will be refused until it is done.

401.description: Unknown email or wrong password. Deliberately does not distinguish the two.

post.description:
Served by Better Auth (ADR-0016). Deletes the session row and clears the cookie, so replaying the cookie fails rather than working until the token would have expired.

Signing out with no session reports success rather than an error: there is nothing to revoke, and nothing the caller could do differently.

get.summary: List the Identity Providers the login page offers
get.description: Enabled Providers only, and only the fields a login button needs. Unauthenticated, as it must be — it is read by visitors who have no session (ADR-0013). An instance with none configured returns an empty list, and its login page is exactly what it was before.

post.summary: Begin a login through an Identity Provider
post.description: Served by Better Auth (ADR-0016). Answers with the provider's authorization URL for the browser to navigate to, and persists this login's PKCE verifier and CSRF nonce as a `verifications` row — server-side, not in memory, which is why a login survives the auth instance being rebuilt (ADR-0019).

provider.description: The Provider's kind, which is its identity (ADR-0017). Must be configured and enabled.

callbackURL.description: Where to land after signing in, as a path within this Registry.

200.description: The authorization URL to navigate to

get.summary: Complete a login an Identity Provider has returned
get.description:
Served by Better Auth (ADR-0016). One path per kind rather than the single shared callback earlier versions used, so each provider console registers `<PUBLIC_URL>/api/auth/callback/<kind>`.

Before any claim is trusted, the returned state must match what was stored for this flow. The login is then refused unless the Provider is enabled and the organisation matches the Provider's permitted one — Google's `hd` claim, Entra's `tid` claim, or, for GitHub, membership returned by `/user/orgs`, since it issues no ID token (ADR-0018). Matched on what the Provider asserts, never on the email address's suffix.

An email matching an existing User signs into them, whatever role they hold; one matching none creates a reader with no password. Every refusal redirects back to the login page with the same coarse reason — which check failed goes to the logs and only there.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: The Provider that returned this login.

get.description: Requires at least the admin role.

post.description:
Requires at least the admin role. The Registry generates the initial password and returns it once — there is no email delivery. The new User must change it before they can do anything else.

`role` accepts `reader`, `writer`, or `admin` only — never `superadmin`, which exists on exactly one User and is set only by `/setup`.

201.description: Created. `initial_password` is shown once and is not recoverable.

409.description: A User with that email already exists

get.description: Also the CLI's identity command: it distinguishes a wrong Registry location from a rejected Token. The role is resolved on this request, not read from the credential.

put.description: Clears `must_change_password`. Permitted while that flag is set — this is the route that resolves it.

get.description: Secrets are never included. `last_used_at` is how a dead Token is identified. Nested under the owner because a User may only ever manage their own.

post.description: The secret is returned exactly once and stored only as a hash. Tokens do not expire; revoke by deleting. A Token carries no role of its own — its owner's current role is resolved on every request, so a demotion applies to existing Tokens immediately.

name.description: A display name, so a Token can be recognised later.

201.description: Minted. `secret` will never be shown again.

delete.description: The next request bearing it fails.

404.description: No such Token belonging to you

patch.description: Requires at least the admin role. Refused on the Superadmin's own User (see 409). Takes effect on that User's next request, including requests bearing their existing Tokens.

delete.description: Requires at least the admin role. Refused on the Superadmin's own User (see 409). Ends their access and deletes their Tokens. Skills they published remain, and attribution survives through the publisher email snapshot.

get.summary: List, search, filter, and sort Skills
get.description: Reads from the `skill_directory` view (ticket 23, docs/data-model.md), not `skills` directly. Defaults to sorted by install count, descending. With `q`, results are additionally full-text matched over name, description, and publisher — `sort_by`/`sort_order` still govern the order even then; there is no separate relevance ranking. Stemming does not substring-match, and hyphenated names tokenise per word — both expected, not defects. Unauthenticated (ADR-0013).

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Full-text search phrase, matched against name, description, and publisher. Supports quoted phrases and `-exclusions`. Omitted or empty returns the ordinary list.

parameters.name: tag_id
parameters.description: Repeatable. Narrows to Skills carrying at least one of the given Tag ids (any-match). Omitted returns Skills regardless of Tags.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description: Governs ordering unconditionally, even with `q` set. Invalid values are rejected with a field-named validation error.

parameters.name: sort_order
parameters.description: Invalid values are rejected with a field-named validation error.

put.description:
Create or replace, idempotent by name: publishing an existing Skill replaces it whoever published it first, and `published_by` and `published_at` become whoever published it last (ADR-0002).

The row is written first and an upload target returned. The caller then writes the Artifact to that target directly. Until it does, the Skill lists and reads but its Artifact cannot be retrieved.

`name` comes from the path; the caller parses it out of `SKILL.md` frontmatter. The API validates it against the same rules the shared module applies, but does not read the Artifact to confirm they agree.

`license`, `compatibility`, `metadata`, and `allowed_tools` are optional, but are validated exactly as strictly as `description` and `body` when present — any one of them failing rejects the whole publish, naming the specific field and rule (ADR-0009). Publishing always writes all four (a validated value, or null when absent), so a republish that no longer sets a field clears it. `tags` cannot be set through this endpoint at all — see `PUT /skills/{id}/tags`.

body.description: The `SKILL.md` content below the frontmatter. Rendered through an allowlist sanitiser, never trusted as markup.

metadata.description: From the SKILL.md frontmatter, a mapping of string keys to string values. Optional.

allowed_tools.description: From the SKILL.md frontmatter. Optional; internal grammar unvalidated (experimental in the specification).

200.description: The Skill row was created or replaced. Write the Artifact to `upload` next.

get.description: An exact-name read, for resolving `name` to `id` — the web keeps `/skills/<name>` as its own browser URL and needs this to land a reader there with nothing already cached (a bookmark, a shared link, a refresh). Not full-text search: `GET /skills?q=` ranks by recency and caps at one page, so it cannot guarantee finding an existing Skill by exact name, and Postgres's stopword handling can make it return nothing at all for a name that happens to be one. Unauthenticated (ADR-0013).

An exact-id read. Does not go through full-text search. The web keeps `/skills/<name>` as its own browser URL and resolves `name` to `id` itself before calling this — see `GET /skills/by-name/{name}`. Unauthenticated (ADR-0013).

delete.description: Requires at least the admin role. Removes the row and the Artifact permanently — there is no version history and no soft delete. Recovery is bucket versioning in object storage (ADR-0002). Succeeds even when the Artifact was never uploaded.

204.description: Deleted. The name is immediately available to publish again.

403.description: Readers and writers cannot delete a Skill

get.description: Records one Install, then redirects to a presigned read location valid for about a minute. Callers must follow redirects. Unauthenticated — anyone who can reach the Registry may retrieve an Artifact (ADR-0013). The response body is the zip, named after the Skill. A caller that sends `Accept: application/json` gets the Skill itself back instead alongside `url` to fetch the Artifact from, rather than a redirect; this is for a caller (the web app's own Download control) that needs to know the request succeeded before navigating there itself. Either representation records the same one Install. `installs` on that Skill reflects the last periodic refresh, not necessarily this request's own Install (ADR-0012).

parameters.name: Accept
parameters.description: Request the Skill-plus-url representation instead of the default redirect.

200.description: The Skill, plus a presigned url to fetch the Artifact from — returned instead of redirecting when the request sent `Accept: application/json`

url.description: Short-lived presigned read URL for the Artifact

302.description: Redirect to the presigned location — the default representation

Location.description: Short-lived presigned read URL for the Artifact

404.description: No such Skill, or its Artifact was never uploaded

put.description: Requires at least the writer role — the same bar as publishing. A full replace, not incremental: the given names become exactly this Skill's Tags, and any Tag it previously carried that isn't in the list is detached (never deleted from the catalog itself, ADR-0011). Each name is normalised (trimmed, lowercased) and resolved to an existing catalog Tag or a newly created one — this is the only way a brand new Tag comes into existence. A name repeated in the list, even under different casing, still resolves to one Tag.

tags.description: The full desired set of tag names, by name — not by id.

200.description: The Skill's resolved Tags after the replace

403.description: Readers cannot edit a Skill's Tags

get.description: Every Tag in the Registry, alphabetical by name — registry-wide, not scoped to any one Skill (ADR-0011). What a tag editor's autocomplete filters against.

patch.description: Requires at least the admin role — stricter than replacing a Skill's Tags, because a rename reaches every Skill carrying this Tag, not just one (ADR-0011). Every reference is by id, so nothing but this Tag's `name` column changes. Conflict detection relies on the database's own unique constraint, so two concurrent renames to the same name can't both succeed.

403.description: Only Admins may rename a Tag

409.description: A different Tag already holds this name

post.summary: Read a Skill's files from a GitHub repository the caller can see
post.description:
Requires at least the writer role. Fetches a folder from a GitHub repository — **private ones included** — using the calling writer's own GitHub OAuth token, and returns its files for the browser to publish through the usual pipeline (ADR-0020).

The body carries the repository's parts and deliberately **no URL**: the server builds every GitHub request itself from these fields, so this route cannot be aimed at another host. The browser parses the pasted URL and sends the result; every part is re-validated here.

Public repositories do not need this. The browser fetches those anonymously and always has (ADR-0010); the interface only falls back to this route when the anonymous attempt cannot see the repository. Nothing here writes to GitHub — every request it makes is a `GET`.

ref.description: Branch, tag, or commit. `null` uses the repository's default branch.

path.description: The folder within the repository, `""` for its root. No leading or trailing slash, and no `.` or `..` segment.

200.description: The folder's files, at paths relative to the folder itself

403.description: The caller is a reader; importing exists to publish

409.description: The caller has no linked GitHub account (`github_not_connected`) — they should sign in with GitHub once

502.description: GitHub refused the request, the folder is empty or invisible to that writer, or it is larger than a Skill may be (`github_import_failed`)

get.description: Requires at least the admin role. Includes disabled Providers, and never includes a client secret.

post.description:
Requires at least the admin role. At most one Provider per kind (ADR-0017). A Provider may be created enabled, but only with a permitted organisation set — with just-in-time provisioning that gate is the only control on who gets an account (ADR-0015).

There is no issuer URL to supply: Better Auth knows each kind's endpoints (ADR-0016), so what an Admin configures is the credential pair and the organisation to admit.

kind.description: The Provider's identity, and immutable after creation (ADR-0017).

client_secret.description: Stored as given, and never returned by any response.

permitted_organisations.description: Organisations this Provider admits — Workspace domains, Entra tenant ids, or GitHub organisation logins by kind. A login is admitted if it matches any one of them, case-insensitively. An empty array means no organisation check runs at all and everyone the provider authenticates gets a reader account (ADR-0021).

409.description: An Identity Provider of that kind is already configured (`kind_taken`)

patch.description:
Requires at least the admin role, and is also how a Provider is enabled and disabled. `kind` cannot be changed: it is the Provider's identity (ADR-0017), so altering it would silently repoint a live configuration rather than configure a second one. Omitting `client_secret` leaves the stored one untouched, which is what lets a Provider be edited without its secret ever being read back.

Changes reach logins by two routes, and the difference matters (ADR-0019): `enabled` and `permitted_organisations` are read on every login and take effect immediately, while new credentials take effect once the auth instance is rebuilt on the next request to its routes. A stale instance can therefore fail a login through a Provider added moments ago, but can never admit someone a disabled Provider should have refused.

There is deliberately no delete route. Disabling is how a Provider is taken out of service — deleting one would lock out everyone who signs in through it over a mistyped click.

permitted_organisations.description: Organisations this Provider admits — Workspace domains, Entra tenant ids, or GitHub organisation logins by kind. A login is admitted if it matches any one of them, case-insensitively. An empty array means no organisation check runs at all and everyone the provider authenticates gets a reader account (ADR-0021).

cookieAuth.name: session
cookieAuth.description: Signed session cookie, http-only, secure, strictly same-site. Carries only the User's id; the role is resolved from the database on every request (ADR-0005). Cannot be revoked before expiry.

bearerAuth.description: A Token, used by the CLI. Looked up by hash on every request; revocable immediately.

SkillName.name: name
SkillName.description: The Skill's name, from its `SKILL.md` frontmatter.

ExternalLoginRedirect.description: A redirect. On success, to the post-login destination with a session cookie set; on any failure, to `/login?error=…` with no session issued. Failures are deliberately not distinguished from one another — the person at the other end can act no differently either way, and naming the check that failed would tell an attacker which one they tripped. The reason reaches the logs.

IdentityProviderNotFound.description: No Identity Provider by that id

Unauthenticated.description: No valid session or Token. The web interface treats this as an expired session, discards cached state, and returns to login.

AdminOnly.description: Requires at least the admin role (admin or the superadmin)

ValidationFailed.description: The request failed a validation rule. `code` names the rule and `field` names what broke it, so the CLI and the web interface can report the same specific reason.

SuperadminProtected.description: Refused: this is the Superadmin. Their role is permanent and their account can never be changed or removed.

Role.description: reader: browse, search, read, retrieve Artifacts. writer: also publish, including replacing any Skill. admin: also delete Skills and manage readers and writers. superadmin: also create and manage Admins. There is exactly one superadmin — set once at `/setup` and never reassigned — so it is never a valid value in a request body; see AssignableRole.

AssignableRole.description: The roles a request body may assign to a User. `superadmin` is excluded on purpose: it is set exactly once, by `/setup`, and no route ever grants, changes, or removes it afterwards.

must_change_password.description: True only for a User holding a password that was generated for them and not yet replaced. Meaningful only where a password exists — a User who authenticates through an identity provider has none (ADR-0007).

Publisher.description: Who last published a Skill. `email` is a snapshot taken at publish time and is always present; `user_id` and the names are null once that User has been removed.

SkillDirectoryEntry.description: One row of `GET /skills` (ticket 23), sourced from the `skill_directory` view — deliberately not SkillSummary: `published_by_name` in place of the full Publisher object, and `updated_at` in place of `published_at`. `GET /skills/{id}` and `by-name/{name}` are unaffected and still return SkillSummary/Skill.

published_by_name.description: A display-name snapshot taken at publish time (docs/data-model.md) — does not update if that User later renames themselves.

updated_at.description: When this Skill was last published, republished, or otherwise changed — not when it was first published (`published_at`, only on the detail read).

installs.description: Same field, same lag caveat as SkillSummary.installs (ADR-0012).

id.description: Stable identity for reading, deleting, and downloading this Skill — generated once, on first publish, and never changes across republishes of the same name. `name` remains how a Skill is published.

license.description: From the SKILL.md frontmatter. Null when the Skill never set it.

compatibility.description: From the SKILL.md frontmatter. Null when the Skill never set it.

metadata.description: From the SKILL.md frontmatter, a mapping of string keys to string values. Null when the Skill never set it.

allowed_tools.description: From the SKILL.md frontmatter. Null when the Skill never set it.

tags.description: Registry-owned, never parsed from or written into SKILL.md (ADR-0008), and never set by publishing — see `PUT /skills/{id}/tags`. Each Tag is drawn from the registry-wide catalog (ADR-0011); empty until something attaches one.

installs.description: How many times this Skill has been installed — a download today, and eventually a CLI install too. 0 until the first one is ever recorded, never null. Reflects the last periodic refresh of the underlying materialized view (ADR-0012), not necessarily every Install recorded so far — this can lag reality by a short interval.

body.description: The `SKILL.md` content below the frontmatter, as supplied by the publisher. Sanitise before rendering.

UploadTarget.description: Where to write the Artifact. A presigned location on object storage — the bytes do not pass through this API.

headers.description: Headers that must be sent verbatim for the presigned signature to verify.

secret.description: Shown once. Never cached by the web interface, and stored only as a hash by the Registry.

Tag.description: A catalog Tag: a stable id plus its current name, shared by every Skill that carries it — renaming one (PATCH /tags/{id}) is visible everywhere it's attached, since every reference is by id, not name (ADR-0011).

name.description: Always stored already lowercased and trimmed.

PublicIdentityProvider.description: What an unauthenticated visitor sees on the login page: enough to draw a button and start a flow, and nothing else. Must never grow a field that could carry a credential.

kind.description: The Provider's identity, and what a login is started against (ADR-0017).

display_name.description: Shown on the login page as "Continue with …".

IdentityProvider.description: An Admin's view of a configured Identity Provider. `client_secret` is deliberately absent from this and every other response: it is written and never read back, so no response can leak it, not even to the Admin who set it.

permitted_organisations.description: The organisations allowed to sign in: Workspace domains (Google `hd`), tenant ids (Entra `tid`), or GitHub organisation logins. A login is admitted if what the Provider asserts matches any one of them, case-insensitively — a claim for the first two, a live `/user/orgs` check for GitHub, which issues no ID token (ADR-0018) — and never against the email address's suffix. An empty array is a configuration rather than a blank: no check runs, and everyone the provider authenticates gets a reader account here (ADR-0021).

enabled.description: Whether the login page offers it and logins through it are accepted. Disabling is how a Provider is taken out of service; there is no delete.

code.description: A stable machine-readable identifier for what went wrong — for validation failures, the specific rule that failed.

field.description: The field or file that broke the rule, when there is one.
